name: STAR
question: In adults with overactive bladder, how does flexible-dose solifenacin compare with fixed-dose tolterodine ER for symptom improvement and tolerability?

arms.label: Solifenacin 5 mg daily, with optional increase to 10 mg

design.population: Adults with overactive bladder syndrome treated at European study sites.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy randomized noninferiority trial
design.locator: 2005 PubMed abstract, Methods; 2007 report, publisher Methods; PMCPA Code of Practice Review 2006, pp35-36 (randomized counts and primary-test design)

verdictNote: Primary frequency endpoint met noninferiority; secondary urgency, incontinence, and pad use favored solifenacin.
takeaway: In STAR, the per-protocol set (525 solifenacin, 524 tolterodine ER) met noninferiority for micturitions per 24 hours at 12 weeks (P = 0.004); full-analysis mean reductions were 2.45 versus 2.24, and urgency, incontinence, and pad use also favored solifenacin.

reports.label: Initial report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed and Crossref, September 2005 print issue; exact online publication date unverified
reports.citation: Chapple CR, Martinez-Garcia R, Selvaggi L, et al. "A Comparison of the Efficacy and Tolerability of Solifenacin Succinate and Extended Release Tolterodine at Treating Overactive Bladder Syndrome: Results of the STAR Trial." *Eur Urol.* 2005;48(3):464-470. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2005.05.015

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to endpoint over 12 weeks in the full analysis set; noninferiority tested in the per-protocol population
results.note: The -0.21 difference is calculated from rounded full-analysis-set means (578 solifenacin, 599 tolterodine). The separate per-protocol noninferiority test included 525 solifenacin and 524 tolterodine recipients (95% CI -0.48 to 0.10; P = 0.004).
results.locator: Primary report PDF pp 466-467, Statistical methods and Results

results.note: The abstract reports larger reductions in urgency, overall and urgency incontinence, and pad use with solifenacin, and more patients achieving continence; no arm values are given.

harms.label: Adverse-event discontinuation
harms.note: The abstract describes discontinuations as comparable and low, without group counts. Most adverse events were mild to moderate.

delivery.label: Dose adjustment

values.exp: 5 mg daily; optional increase to 10 mg after 4 weeks

delivery.note: Patients in both blinded groups could request an increase, but only solifenacin could actually be increased under approved labeling.

reports.label: Starting-dose subanalysis
reports.citation: Chapple CR, Fianu-Jonsson A, Indig M, et al. "Treatment Outcomes in the STAR Study: A Subanalysis of Solifenacin 5 mg and Tolterodine ER 4 mg." *Eur Urol.* 2007;52(4):1195-1203. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2007.05.027
reports.followUp: 4-week randomized starting-dose comparison; endpoint (12 weeks or last clinic visit) in patients who chose not to increase dose
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods 2.1 and Results 3.2, pp 1196–1198

results.measure: Mean reduction from baseline before the dose-increase option; randomized starting-dose full analysis set (578 solifenacin, 599 tolterodine ER)
results.note: Solifenacin minus tolterodine change is calculated from rounded arm means; Table 1 reports the superiority comparison as not significant (ns), without an exact P value or confidence interval.
results.locator: Full text, Results 3.1 and Table 1, pp 1197–1198

results.measure: Mean reduction from baseline in episodes per 24 hours at 4 weeks before the dose-increase option; randomized starting-dose full analysis set (578 solifenacin, 599 tolterodine ER)
results.note: Solifenacin-minus-tolterodine change is calculated from rounded arm means; P value is from the reported ANCOVA superiority comparison. No confidence interval is reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods 2.1.2, Results 3.1 and Table 1, pp 1197–1198

results.measure: Mean reduction from baseline in pads per 24 hours at 4 weeks before the dose-increase option; randomized starting-dose full analysis set (578 solifenacin, 599 tolterodine ER)
results.note: Solifenacin-minus-tolterodine change is calculated from rounded arm means; P value is from the reported ANCOVA superiority comparison. No confidence interval is reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods 2.1.2, Results 3.1 and Table 1, pp 1197–1198

results.measure: Mean reduction from baseline in episodes per 24 hours at endpoint (12 weeks or last clinic visit) in patient-selected full-analysis-set subgroups (290 solifenacin, 283 tolterodine ER)
results.note: The no-dose-increase subgroups arose by patient choice after week 4; endpoint comparisons were descriptive, without formal superiority testing.
results.locator: Full text, Methods 2.1.1–2.1.2, Table 2, Table 3 and Fig. 2, pp 1197–1200

harms.locator: Full text, Results 3.3.1 and Table 4, p 1200

harms.locator: Full text, Results 3.3.1 and Table 4, p 1200

delivery.locator: Full text, Methods 2.1.1 and Table 2, pp 1197–1199
